title: Eagles WRs coach Aaron Moorehead on the size of the WRs: "Are you playing big? Are you playing tough? That's the big thing. And so I look over the last couple years: We weren't the tallest group, but we had guys that were tough, we had guys that played hard, and you got to continue to do that. And this offense is doing your 1/11, but a lot of it is about toughness. A lot of it is about being in the exact place you're supposed to be. It's about being football smart. It's about playing tough, and then obviously about finishing making plays. "We've got guys. Like, DeVonta's 170 pounds, but he don't play that way. He plays tougher than that. He plays bigger than that. He always has. Darius Cooper's a bigger guy, stronger guy. He did that. He played that role for us last year, and you can see some of the contested catches he's made all camp. He showed he's been able to be the blocker over the course of last year and through camp. He's done a great job. (Dontayvion Wicks) is not a 220-pound guy, but he plays that way. So again, there's different ways you can make it work."

Trying to find that right balance. The ones that have gone 95 need to have consequences for that." More from Byrne on state of college sports: "When the House settlement happened, we were hoping it was going to create some guidelines and rules that we were all going to follow. Unfortunately the enforcement end of that one was very, very slow to come out of the gates. People didn’t think there were a whole lot of rules that came along with it. I think they’re actually making some progress, the College Sports Commission on that, so we’ll see hopefully in a couple months or two."

title: Asked #49ers DE Nick Bosa about his timeline for recovery in this camp. He gave a detailed answer about ramping up too quickly and dealing with patella issues. Here's his full response: "I'm not going to go back too far because every recovery there's ups and downs, but it was a long road. There's some stuff I dealt with, with that patella tendon, and then I kind of ramped it a little too fast with the football stuff a month ago or whatever it was. And that kind of told me to back off. I've just been trying to get it as strong and myself as confident as I can to where I could rip the bandaid off and go to team stuff today. Because once you get into team, there's no reservations, there's no compensation, like there's no governor. So yeah, I felt that today. I remember my last ACL, there was a couple moments where you just have to go and you're kind of hoping for the best. Obviously it's not going to be like anything crazy is going to happen, but you hope that your body is going to respond the way that you prepared it to. And there's a couple moments today where that happened. So I'm just going to try and keep building, not get too up about it, but it was a great day."

title: Remember in the spring when Dennis Allen said that better coaching would yield better results from the Bears' pass rush? Here's where Allen said he's seen improvement in that area: "Typically to affect the quarterback with a rush, unless you're Myles Garrett or Von Miller back in the day, it's really right at about 3.1 seconds...Prior to that, you've got to affect the quarterback with your coverage, meaning you've got to get him to have to go to his second or third read. And so, if the ball's getting out in 2.5 seconds, statistically you're not going to see a lot of sacks, a lot of hurries, a lot of hits. Sacks, hurries and hits need to come when the quarterback has to reset, and that typically is going to be 3 to 3.2 seconds. I felt like when the quarterback had to go to a second or third read, I felt like more consistently we were able to to affect him."

title: There has been a lot of talk all summer about a lot of Bears defensive tackles. But there hasn't been a lot of buzz about Kentavius Street's strong camp. So I asked Dennis Allen about him and he lit up. "Quite honestly, I think he was the most-productive tackle we had throughout the course of training camp. He's got the suddenness and the explosiveness off the ball that we're looking for to create penetration and disrupt the line of scrimmage. He's really taken to the things that Jeremy (Garrett), Bill (Johnson), Zach (Cable), all those guys are coaching and how we want to play that position."
